Issued at 1222 AM EST Wed Nov 11 2026

             -----------Synoptic Overview-----------

A split flow regime persists over the Eastern U.S. Of immediate
concern for Central Florida is the subtropical jet extending along
the Northern Gulf Coast, and specifically an embedded shortwave
over the Ark-La-Tex region. This disturbance is forecast to move
eastward today. As it reaches N Fla by evening, the environment
will become more favorable for synoptic-scale ascent.

Moisture is slowly returning, evidenced by scattered returns
on KMLB radar. By this afternoon, PWAT values are forecast to
jump to 140% or more of normal from near Orlando and especially
southward. Relatively steep mid-level lapse rates are also expected,
contributing to moderate instability over the southern half of
the peninsula later today. Finally, the nearby jet should provide
effective shear of 30-40 kt. By Thursday, thermodynamics will
become less favorable for deep convection as deep moisture is
slowly pushed southward.

Meanwhile, the polar jet is beginning to amplify. Transient but
stout high-latitude blocking has developed this morning, with
well-above-normal 500 mb heights from the Northwest Territories
to Greenland. High confidence persists that meridional upper
flow will overtake the nation late this week and through much of
the weekend. Deep troughs are expected to form over the Eastern
U.S. and just off the Pacific Coast as a ridge builds over the
Rockies. On the leading edge of the developing trough over the East,
low pressure will strengthen as it passes from the Ohio Valley to
the Mid-Atlantic through late Thursday. Its trailing cold front
should pass through Florida on Thursday night.

Cold, continental high pressure should build southward out of
Canada on Friday. Chilly northwesterly flow will develop over the
Southeast and Florida from Friday into Saturday, allowing 925 mb
temps to fall to between +6 and +11 deg C as PWATs tumble to 30%
of normal by early Saturday. The cold, East Coast trough should
slowly weaken and push toward the Canadian Maritimes by early
next week. High pressure follows close behind, with a deepening
layer of brisk onshore flow resuming from Sunday into early next
week. This will quickly reverse the cold advection and begin a
moderating trend over the peninsula.

The Pacific jet is expected to remain active with multiple
disturbances reaching the West Coast over the next several days.
As the high-latitude block breaks down, the pattern is likely to
become progressive next week. At least half of the physics-based 
ensemble members, along with the ECMWF-AIFS mean, suggest one of 
these features will undercut a ridge over the High Plains and 
reach the Southeast U.S. by Monday or Tuesday. Modest moisture 
advection is also anticipated, suggesting a return to unsettled 
conditions by that time.

Ensemble agreement and forecast confidence are high through the
weekend but decrease into next week.

             -------Sensible Weather & Impacts-------

Today - Tonight...

A weak disturbance sparked a few showers last evening and early
this morning, but this activity should be pushing off into the
Atlantic. Except for isolated showers, we expect generally quiet
conditions through early afternoon.

As mentioned in the overview, at least marginally favorable
parameters will exist for storm development this afternoon and
evening, especially south of Orlando to the Treasure Coast. The
question will be whether an area of forcing associated with the
subtropical jet will effectively overlap with the deeper moisture
and instability. Guidance handles this with 30-40% rain and storm
chances late in the day.

If storms can manage to form, there is still a low and conditional
strong to severe storm threat. With nearly unidirectional wind
profiles, gusty winds to 50-60 mph and hail to around quarter
size would be the primary hazards. Locally, heavy rain will occur
beneath the storms, but overall storm motions should mitigate a
flooding risk.

Highs today will be the warmest of the next week or so, generally
in the low to mid 80s. Most areas should return to dry conditions
later tonight with mild temps persisting.

Thursday - Friday...

Moisture gets squeezed southward on Thursday as westerly flow mixes
down some drier air across the northern half of the state. Shower
chances (20-40%) are relegated to the Treasure Coast. We expect
quite a bit of cloud cover as a cold front approaches. Highs should
reach 75-80 degrees.

The cold front makes its pass through Central Florida on Thursday
night. By Friday afternoon, it will be well south of here. Clearing
skies are forecast on Friday, with temps trending below normal
in the low to mid 70s. Breezy northwest winds will develop with
gusts 15-25 mph.

Weekend...
